svg.aria-label: Frame 2 of 3: the actual interleaved per-element trace for the same pipeline, printed line by line for the first three stake reservations of 4.20, 2.10 and 6.00 — filter, map and forEach for each reservation run to completion before the next reservation is pulled from the source, proving vertical fusion through the whole pipeline for one element at a time.
svg.text: FRAME 2 / 3 — THE ACTUAL INTERLEAVED PER-ELEMENT TRACE
Same source code as frame 1 — measured JDK 21 output, unchanged.
MEASURED — one Reservation is fully pushed through before the next is pulled
rejected — 2.10 < 4.20, map/forEach never called for it
Reading order top to bottom is the pull order, not the declaration order:
filter(4.20) → map(4.20) → forEach(4.20) → filter(2.10) → filter(6.00) → map(6.00) → forEach(6.00)
No "map" line ever appears for 2.10 — filter's false short-circuits that element at stage 1,
it never reaches stage 2 or 3. This is what "vertical fusion" means: one element rides the
whole 3-stage sink chain in one call stack before the source is asked for the next element.
